skill.name: security-compliance
skill.description: Guide security and compliance teams through risk assessment, security architecture, incident response, and audit readiness. Includes SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and secure SDLC references.
skill.summary: Assess risks, plan controls, prepare audits, and improve security operations with structured compliance workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from defensive security education, examples, and helper scripts. I confirmed the API JWT example because it hardcodes a SECRET_KEY placeholder in best-practices guidance. I also found one dual-use penetration testing workflow that needs explicit authorization guardrails.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the literal SECRET_KEY sample with environment or secrets manager retrieval and mark sample values non-production.
Add written authorization, scope, and no-unauthorized-access guardrails before offensive testing sections.
Label scripts as examples, require local review, and document credential handling and output paths.

content.value_statement: Security teams need clear workflows for risk, controls, incidents, and audits. This skill provides structured guidance, templates, and scripts for defensible security compliance work.
actual_capabilities: Build risk registers using qualitative and quantitative risk methods.
Prioritize vulnerabilities with CVSS scores and business context.
Plan SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS controls.
Draft incident response workflows, tabletop exercises, and after action reports.
Guide secure SDLC reviews using OWASP Top 10 practices.
Use example scripts for CSV risk and vulnerability reports.
limitations: Does not replace legal, audit, or regulator advice.
Requires user-provided assets, controls, policies, and scope.
Example scripts need review before production use.
Offensive testing guidance requires written authorization and defined scope.

use_cases.title: Plan compliance readiness
use_cases.description: Map required controls, evidence, owners, and timelines for an upcoming audit.

use_cases.title: Prepare incident response
use_cases.description: Create response steps, tabletop scenarios, and after action improvements for common incidents.

use_cases.title: Improve application security
use_cases.description: Review secure coding practices, CI/CD checks, API security, and OWASP Top 10 gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Start a risk register
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple risk register for our product. Ask me for assets, threats, likelihood, impact, owners, and due dates.

prompt_templates.title: Map audit controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare for SOC 2. Build a control checklist with owners, evidence sources, test steps, and gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design an incident exercise
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ransomware tabletop exercise for a 90 minute session. Include injects, expected decisions, and improvement actions.

prompt_templates.title: Crosswalk frameworks
prompt_templates.prompt: Crosswalk our current controls against SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and PCI DSS. Highlight overlaps, gaps, and evidence reuse.

output_examples.input: I need SOC 2 evidence for MFA enforcement.
output: Control objective and owner for MFA enforcement.
Evidence sources from identity, cloud, and access logs.
Quarterly test steps and expected results.
Exceptions, remediation owners, and retention guidance.
Priority levels based on CVSS and business exposure.
Patch deadlines tied to risk severity.
Rationale for internet-facing and sensitive systems.
A timed scenario with business and technical injects.
Decision points for containment, recovery, legal, and communications.
Expected evidence, roles, and after action improvements.

best_practices: Define scope, owners, and evidence expectations before using any template.
Review all scripts and commands in a test environment first.
Keep compliance outputs tied to real systems, controls, and business risks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat templates as legal or audit signoff.
Do not run response or testing commands outside approved scope.
Do not paste real secrets, tokens, or regulated data into prompts.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for security, compliance, SOC, AppSec, and risk teams that need structured security workflows.

faq.question: Can it complete an audit for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize controls, evidence, and gaps, but auditors and legal teams make final decisions.

faq.question: Does it include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python examples for risk and vulnerability reports that require local review before use.

faq.question: Can I use it for penetration testing?
faq.answer: Only for authorized testing with written scope, rules of engagement, and stakeholder approval.

faq.question: Which frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: It references SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FedRAMP, OWASP, NIST, and CIS concepts.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
